newsitem.title: UK: Copper nears $2,400 on LME, spread hits $200 back.
newsitem.headline: Copper nears $2,400 on LME, spread hits $200 back.

text.p: Copper prices continued to climb during early Thursday LME trading, with three months values nearing $2,400 and the cash/threes spread hitting $200 backwardation.
Traders said the tightness continued to strangle market prompt dates between late April and early May - a situation which is likely to come to a head next week.
The build up in tightness partly reflects the late January 1997 spike in backwardations, with major short positions being rolled forward from then.
Long positions are said to be dominated by investment houses, while shorts being caught are believed to be both speculative and natural trade hedgers.

The scenario is also being underscored by a combination of fundamental factors such as the labour disputes in Chile, the Kennecott smelter shut-down and the forthcoming seasonal slowdown in Russian cathode shipments.

Three months prices hit a high of $2,397 a tonne before settling at $2,390, a $23 advance from the previous kerb close. The cash/threes backwardation was straddling $200, against $160/170 on Wednesday.
The action in the other metals was less intense and price movements less extreme.
"It is all copper interest - the others are not doing much," one said.
Aluminium managed to reach a high of $1,610 before settling back to $1,603, up just $1.50 from yesterday's kerb with the market hitting overhead resistance.
Traders said another 3,250-tonne stock decline failed to excite the market much, with prices somewhat reluctant to over-extend.
"Copper is on its own at the moment - it has a reason to go up, while aluminium doesn't," another trader said.
Zinc gained $3 at at $1,286 while nickel rose to $7,530, up $55.
Tin drifted lower to $5,755, off $45, while lead and alloy were indicated at steady levels of $638/640 and $1,490/1,495 respectively.
